topic: Host-side per-operation overhead in q4 decode: direct host-phase measurement (no per-dispatch GPU timestamps), cross-checked, plus a recorded-command-replay prototype
host: jwm1-linux, Apple M1 (G13G B1), Honeykrisp, linux-asahi 7.1.6
base: d1dfaf2b (main-integrate) + wave/HostPathOverhead measurement wheel 12012beb (NEVER MERGED); venv mlx-lm pinned 0.31.3

A_host_phase_trace.what: MLX_OMARCHY_HOST_TRACE: CLOCK_MONOTONIC phase counters in gpu::eval (backend_eval, bookkeeping), dispatch_compute_pipeline (desc_setup/barriers/vkcmd/ensure_recording), submit, completion drain, allocator; plus a monkeypatched mx.eval timer and per-token wall gaps in receipts/2026-09-10-hostpath/hostphases.py. Zero GPU timestamps anywhere.
A_host_phase_trace.digest_gate: gates-off legs reproduce all three canonical digests 9/9 (7fd25a869ff21678 / 4cc08910089477fd / 7da83f06ec9f001d) and 111.67/108.06/96.93 tok/s (-0.8/-1.1/-0.4% vs b6d662a canonical): the instrument is inert when off.

C_replay_prototype.what: MLX_OMARCHY_REPLAY=1: per-dispatch cached command buffers, byte-identical compare of pipeline+bindings+push constants+groups, up to 4 binding-address variants per sequence position (async decode ping-pongs two allocator address sets), chained descriptor pools, one multi-buffer submission per token.
C_replay_prototype.bit_identity: PASS - all 9 replay legs x 3 workloads reproduce the canonical digests exactly.
C_replay_prototype.performance: FAIL - 42.64 tok/s vs 111.67 baseline short (23.45 ms vs 8.955 ms per token, +162%): per-dispatch command-buffer submission fan-out (~282 buffers per token through one vkQueueSubmit) costs far more on Honeykrisp than the host record work it removes. Rejected as a structural fix in this form.

B_tiny_model_floor.status: NOT COMPLETED - tiny build hit mx.save_safetensors std::bad_cast then Module.save_weights path ran out of window; fix path known (cast parameter tree before save). fdinfo GPU accounting does not exist on asahi (verified), so the GPU-busy floor was not directly measured this session.

cpp_phases_ms.note: finest-grain scopes (desc/barriers/vkcmd/ensure) sum to ~2x their container, i.e. steady_clock reads on this kernel cost ~0.4-0.5us each; coarse numbers above are the trustworthy ones. Per-dispatch coarse: C++ Vulkan record+descriptor path is <=0.76 ms/token of an 8.95 ms token (8.5%).

measured_split_per_token_short_32.nodes_and_dispatches: 944.8 eval nodes and 281.7 compute dispatches per token; 2.2 submissions per token
measured_split_per_token_short_32.reading: The host thread is busy essentially the whole token wall: ~6.4 ms Python graph construction + ~2.6 ms C++ eval/submit work; the GPU overlaps inside that. Combined with the prior cross-check microbench on main (eager tiny-add chain 40-58 us/op vs 4.5 us pre-recorded floor) and the dispatch-floor receipt (GPU launch cadence 4.5 us x 282 = 1.27 ms/token), decode on this stack is HOST-paced, not GPU-paced.

hypothesis_verdict.host_share: CONFIRMED in direction: the host owns the token wall; the GPU is not the limiter.
hypothesis_verdict.location_correction: The dominant host term is Python eager graph construction (6.4 of 8.95 ms), NOT the Vulkan descriptor/record path (<=0.76 ms measured). The 28-58us/op eager cadence seen per-op in Python loops amortizes to ~9.5us/node when one eval batches ~945 nodes.
hypothesis_verdict.replay_conclusion: Command-buffer replay alone is bounded by the record+descriptor share (~1.5-1.9 ms/token best case) and the naive per-dispatch implementation loses 2.6x to submission fan-out. The structural fix implied by the measurement is whole-graph capture on the decode step (mx.compile-style capture/replay with buffer rebinding, or a C++ cached decode loop) to remove the Python term first; command-buffer reuse is only worth it AFTER the graph is captured once and resubmitted as few large buffers.
